new.title: Wander the Ottoman houses of Beypazarı
new.desc: Beypazarı preserves roughly 3,000 timber-and-stone Ottoman houses from the 18th and 19th centuries along cobbled lanes. Many now serve as museums, guesthouses and restaurants.
new.tip: Go on a weekday morning to avoid weekend coach crowds; the Alaaddin quarter has the best-kept streets.

new.title: Visit the Turkish Bath Museum in Rüstem Pasha Hamam
new.desc: This 16th-century hamam, attributed to Rüstem Pasha, reopened on 9 June 2012 as a museum of Turkish bath culture. Mannequins and bathing equipment show how the ritual worked.
new.tip: Allow 30 minutes; check opening hours locally as municipal museums often close on Mondays.
new.q: Hamam Müzesi, Rüstem Paşa Hamamı, Beypazarı, Ankara

new.title: Look for black storks in İnözü Valley
new.desc: The İnözü Valley north of Beypazarı is a canyon of rock tombs and cliffs. The Culture and Tourism Ministry records black storks and a lanner falcon pair nesting there.
new.tip: Come in spring or early summer for nesting birds; a car is needed from Beypazarı.

new.title: Spot herons and storks at Nallıhan Bird Paradise
new.desc: An artificial wetland where the Aladağ stream meets Sarıyar Dam, protected as a wildlife area since 2005 over about 425 hectares. About 190 bird species have been recorded, including breeding black storks.
new.tip: Bring binoculars; spring and autumn migration are best. It is about 130 km from Ankara.
new.q: Nallıhan Kuş Cenneti, Davutoğlan, Nallıhan, Ankara

new.title: See Sarıyar Dam lake from the Nallıhan road
new.desc: Sarıyar Dam on the Sakarya River opened in 1959 and forms a long reservoir that hosts over 50,000 wintering water birds some years. Its shoreline is among the quietest in western Ankara province.
new.tip: Stop at the viewpoints on the Beypazarı to Nallıhan road; winter brings the most birds.

new.title: Explore the Gordion Museum at Yassıhöyük
new.desc: The museum documents the Phrygian capital Gordion from the Bronze Age to the Byzantine period and holds a reconstruction of the Midas tumulus tomb interior. A 9th-century BC pebble mosaic lies in the garden.
new.tip: Public transport is poor; hire a taxi from Polatlı or drive. Plan 1.5 hours with the tumulus.

new.title: Walk into the 53 m Midas Tumulus (Tumulus MM)
new.desc: One of Anatolia's largest burial mounds, 53 m high, popularly called the tomb of King Midas though it dates to about 740 BC and probably holds an earlier king. A tunnel leads to the intact timber tomb chamber.
new.tip: Opposite the museum; the tunnel is cool inside, so bring a light layer.

new.title: Climb the Gordion Citadel Mound
new.desc: The citadel mound holds the excavated Phrygian city gate, megara and burnt destruction layer, dug by the University of Pennsylvania. It is where Alexander is said to have cut the Gordian knot.
new.tip: About 2 km west of the museum; wear sturdy shoes and expect little shade.
new.q: Gordion Citadel Mound, Yassıhöyük, Polatlı, Ankara

new.title: Visit the Sakarya Victory Monument at Kartaltepe
new.desc: The monument and museum stand in the Battle of Sakarya National Historic Park, set up in 2015 over the 1921 battlefield. Wikivoyage lists the museum as open Tuesday to Sunday.
new.tip: A car is needed to reach the park sections; allow half a day for several sites.
new.q: Sakarya Zaferi Anıtı, Kartaltepe, Polatlı, Ankara

new.title: Tour the Sakarya Battle Museum in Polatlı
new.desc: Museum and visitor centre of the national historic park telling the 22-day Battle of Sakarya in August and September 1921 during the Turkish War of Independence.
new.tip: Start here for context before visiting the hills; closed on Mondays.
new.q: Sakarya Meydan Muharebesi Müzesi, Polatlı, Ankara

new.title: Stand on Duatepe where the Sakarya line held
new.desc: Duatepe, north of Üçpınar village, was a critical point of the 1921 battle and carries a monument within the historic national park.
new.tip: Quiet spot with a wide plateau view; visit in dry weather as tracks get muddy.

new.title: Climb Kalecik Castle for the vineyard view
new.desc: The ruined hilltop castle above Kalecik town gives the village its name (small castle), and overlooks the Kızılırmak valley vineyards of the Kalecik Karası grape.
new.tip: Go at sunset; the steps are steep and uneven.

new.title: Stroll the old stone houses of Kalecik
new.desc: Kalecik's old quarter climbs the hillside under the castle with traditional Ankara-stone houses and vineyards at the edge of town.
new.tip: Combine with a winery visit; the October grape harvest is the liveliest time.

new.title: Walk through Soğuksu National Park
new.desc: Established on 19 February 1959, Soğuksu is often called Turkey's first national park, with pine and fir forest and both hot and cold springs.
new.tip: Entry fee per car; weekends are crowded, weekdays are calm. It is about 80 km north of Ankara.

new.title: See the Abacı fairy chimneys near Kızılcahamam
new.desc: Volcanic tuff pillars in the Kızılcahamam Geopark area form small fairy chimneys, a modest echo of Cappadocia within two hours of Ankara.
new.tip: Reachable by car; ask locally for the exact track as signage is sparse.

new.title: Look over Çamlıdere Dam lake
new.desc: Çamlıdere Dam supplies Ankara with water and its lake sits among pine forest. Sources list it with Kesikköprü as a fishing reservoir.
new.tip: Weekday visits give quiet shoreline picnics; bring food.

new.title: Hike Aluçdağı Nature Park forests
new.desc: Aluçdağı Nature Park near Çamlıdere protects mountain forest with picnic areas and hiking tracks.
new.tip: Best in late spring and autumn; check road access after rain.

new.title: Walk Güdül's stone-and-timber old houses
new.desc: Güdül, on the old Silk Road route, retains traditional stone-and-timber houses that Hürriyet highlights as an alternative to busier Beypazarı.
new.tip: Quiet and unrestored; a short stop on the way to Beypazarı.

new.title: Stroll Ayaş's old streets
new.desc: Ayaş is a small hill town west of Ankara with Ottoman-era houses and a reputation for its thermal springs.
new.tip: Combine with the Ayaş thermal bath; spring is greenest.

new.title: Watch sunset on the Tuz Gölü salt flats
new.desc: Tuz Gölü (Salt Lake) is Turkey's second-largest lake, a vast shallow salt pan that dries into a white crust each summer. Şereflikoçhisar is the closest town for access.
new.tip: Summer for the white crust, spring for mirror reflections; bring sunglasses.

new.title: See the Şereflikoçhisar salt works
new.desc: Salt is harvested from the lake's pans near Şereflikoçhisar, providing a large share of Turkey's salt.
new.tip: Photograph from the roadside; do not enter working pans without permission.

new.title: Tour the MKE Firearms Industry Museum
new.desc: One of two such museums in Türkiye, with several hundred weapons from the 15th to 20th centuries, linked to Kırıkkale's MKE arms factory. Visits need special authorization.
new.tip: Contact MKE or the local tourism office in advance; photography may be restricted.

new.title: Visit the Hasandede mosque and tomb complex
new.desc: The complex dated to 1605 was restored in 1777 and 1807 and honours the Sufi Hasan Dede, 10 to 12 km from central Kırıkkale.
new.tip: Dress modestly; the tomb is an active pilgrimage site.
new.q: Hasandede Camii ve Türbesi, Hasandede, Kırıkkale

new.title: Cross the Seljuk Çeşnigir Bridge
new.desc: A 13th-century cut-stone bridge on the Kızılırmak, about 110 m long, with three different arch courses.
new.tip: Short roadside stop; combine with the river walk.

new.title: See Keskin's Taş Mektep culture centre
new.desc: Keskin's red Ankara-stone school building now serves as the Hacı Taşan Culture Centre and anchors the old town.
new.tip: Pair with the nearby Bedesten and Greek church.

new.title: Descend into Sulu Cave near Keskin
new.desc: A fossil cave about 27 km from Kırıkkale city with stalactites and a small stream.
new.tip: Wear grippy shoes; ask the municipality about guided access.

new.title: Climb Çankırı Castle and Karatekin Bey's tomb
new.desc: The hilltop fortress overlooks Çankırı and contains the tomb of Seljuk commander Karatekin Bey, who took Kastamonu, Sinop and Çankırı.
new.tip: Evening light on the town is best from the walls.

new.title: Admire the Seljuk Taş Mescit
new.desc: The most important surviving Seljuk building in Çankırı, dated 1235 or 1243 depending on the source, and being restored for Karatekin University.
new.tip: Check whether restoration still limits entry.

new.title: Visit Çankırı Ulu Mosque
new.desc: The city's central Ottoman-era mosque forms the heart of the old town below the castle.
new.tip: Visit outside prayer times.

new.title: Tour the Çankırı Museum
new.desc: The museum shows archaeology and ethnography from the Çankırı area.
new.tip: Closed Mondays; allow an hour.

new.title: Descend into the Çankırı Salt Cave
new.desc: Turkey's largest rock-salt reserve, mined for about 5,000 years and about 18 to 20 km from the city, with parts opened as a show cave.
new.tip: Dress warmly; check it is open as it has had closures.

new.title: Eat Beypazarı güveç at Değirmencioğlu
new.desc: A popular Beypazarı restaurant for local dishes including güveç, the clay-pot lamb and vegetable stew slow-cooked in a wood oven for hours.
new.tip: Order the güveç early as only a few are prepared daily.

new.title: Try wood-oven Beypazarı güveç at Tarihi Güveç Fırını
new.desc: A restaurant praised for the slow-baked Beypazarı güveç and sautéed meat, in the historic centre.
new.tip: Arrive hungry and before afternoon; weekends are busy.

new.title: Eat fresh gözleme at Fatma Teyze in Beypazarı
new.desc: A tiny gözleme spot cited by visitor guides as an authentic stop in the historic quarter.
new.tip: Pair with ayran; go before noon.

new.title: Buy Beypazarı kurusu in the old bazaar
new.desc: Beypazarı kurusu, a buttery biscuit with sesame, chocolate or almond, got geographical indication status in 2013.
new.tip: Buy it fresh from bakeries on the historic bazaar street.

new.title: Taste Kalecik Karası at Vinkara Winery
new.desc: Founded in 2003, Vinkara focuses on native grapes such as Kalecik Karası in the hills near Kalecik, with flight and vertical tastings.
new.tip: Confirm visit hours by phone before driving out.

new.title: Sip Kalecik Karası at Tafali Winery
new.desc: A Kalecik-based winery producing the pale ruby local grape wine.
new.tip: Phone ahead for tastings; October is harvest season.

new.title: Drink Kalecik Karası wine in Kalecik town
new.desc: Kalecik Karası, the geographically marked grape, was rescued from near extinction by Prof. Sabit Ağaoğlu and gives the Kalecik wine tradition its identity.
new.tip: Buy a bottle direct from local producers in the town.

new.title: Have bazlama breakfast near Soğuksu Park
new.desc: Kızılcahamam is known for butter-topped bazlama with gözleme and çörek, served at picnic and forest cafés around the park.
new.tip: Go early on weekends before the crowds.
new.q: Soğuksu Milli Parkı restaurant, Kızılcahamam, Ankara

new.title: Have a lake breakfast in Çamlıdere
new.desc: Çamlıdere is popular for open-air village breakfasts near the dam and forest.
new.tip: Weekends are busy; arrive before 10.
new.q: Çamlıdere Baraj Gölü kahvaltı, Çamlıdere, Ankara

new.title: Eat grilled trout near Kızılcahamam
new.desc: Trout is farmed and served in the pine valleys around Kızılcahamam and Çamlıdere, usually grilled whole.
new.tip: Pick a family-run restaurant on the valley road and ask for fresh grilled alabalık.

new.title: Eat testi kebabı at Derya Lokantası in Çankırı
new.desc: A family-run home-cooking restaurant in the historic centre; Çankırı's signature dish is testi kebabı, meat cooked in a sealed clay pitcher.
new.tip: Ask for the testi to be broken at the table.

new.title: Have a Çankırı breakfast at Çankırı Sofrası
new.desc: A breakfast restaurant listed in travel itineraries serving local pastries like yazma and tava çöreği.
new.tip: Go on weekend mornings.

new.title: Eat kebab at Kervan Kebap Salonu in Çankırı
new.desc: A kebab house in the city centre listed in recent Çankırı itineraries.
new.tip: Order mixed grill with tarhana soup.

new.title: Try Çankırı yumurta tatlısı
new.desc: An egg-based dessert with geographical indication status, long the town's best-known sweet.
new.tip: Buy it fresh at pastry shops near the old town.

new.title: Eat İskender at Ilgaz Park
new.desc: A restaurant in Ilgaz town serving İskender kebab for skiers and hikers.
new.tip: Go at lunch after a morning on the mountain.

new.title: Eat pide at Yeşil Ilgaz in Ilgaz
new.desc: A pide, döner and lahmacun place in Ilgaz town centre.
new.tip: Cheap fill before or after the park.
new.q: Yeşil Ilgaz Pide Salonu, Ilgaz, Çankırı

new.title: Eat tarhana soup in Keskin
new.desc: Keskin's old bazaar area has small restaurants serving the region's fermented tarhana soup.
new.tip: Try one near the Bedesten.

new.title: Watch Beypazarı telkari silverwork being made
new.desc: Beypazarı is known for filigree silver, where fine wire is twisted into jewellery and trays in small workshops.
new.tip: Workshops on the bazaar street welcome visitors; buy directly.
new.q: Tarihi Çarşı gümüş atölyeleri, Beypazarı, Ankara

new.title: Join the Beypazarı carrot harvest
new.desc: Beypazarı produces roughly 40 percent of Turkey's carrots; harvest is at dawn in autumn fields.
new.tip: Visit between September and November; ask a local guide.

new.title: Drive the Sakarya Battle trail
new.desc: The national historic park links monuments across Polatlı and Haymana districts on a driving route.
new.tip: Pick up a map at the visitor centre; allow a day.
new.q: Sakarya Meydan Muharebesi Tarihi Milli Parkı, Polatlı, Ankara

new.title: Soak in Haymana thermal springs
new.desc: Haymana has long been known for its hot springs and thermal baths.
new.tip: Check which pools are open to day visitors.

new.title: Take the Kızılcahamam thermal waters
new.desc: Kızılcahamam's hot springs feed several spa hotels and public baths near Soğuksu Park.
new.tip: Spa hotels sell day passes.

new.title: Try the Çamlıdere Adventure Park
new.desc: A rope and zip-line park in forest near Çamlıdere dam.
new.tip: Book ahead on weekends.

new.title: Ride horses in Kızılcahamam forest
new.desc: Guided horse trekking routes run through the Kızılcahamam and Çamlıdere area.
new.tip: Book with a local stable.

new.title: Ski at Elmadağ Ski Centre
new.desc: A small ski centre on the northern slopes of Elmadağ, about 26 km from Ankara, with a season from January to March.
new.tip: Check snow cover before going.

new.title: Relax in Ayaş hot springs
new.desc: Ayaş's thermal springs are on tourism lists of places near Ankara.
new.tip: Go midweek.

new.title: Walk the Kalecik vineyards
new.desc: Vineyards climb the valley slopes below the castle.
new.tip: Best late spring to early autumn.

new.title: Walk the Kızılırmak at Karaahmetli Nature Park
new.desc: A riverside park and walking path near Kırıkkale.
new.tip: Picnic spot; free.

new.title: Ski at Ilgaz Mountain
new.desc: Ilgaz has a small winter ski area on the national park slopes.
new.tip: Check conditions; winter only.
new.q: Ilgaz Dağı Kayak Merkezi, Ilgaz, Çankırı

new.title: Hike the Ilgaz National Park trails
new.desc: Trails run through forest and alpine meadows on the Ilgaz massif.
new.tip: Best May to October.
new.q: Ilgaz Dağı Milli Parkı, Ilgaz, Çankırı

new.title: Bathe at Kurşunlu thermal springs
new.desc: Kurşunlu's hot springs are a regional spa destination in Çankırı province.
new.tip: Check hours.

new.title: Cycle along the Kızılırmak in Kırıkkale
new.desc: A riverside route links Seljuk bridges and parks.
new.tip: Bring a bike.

new.title: Walk the Gordion archaeological trail
new.desc: Walk from the museum past the tumuli to the citadel mound.
new.tip: Allow 2 hours.

new.title: Browse Keskin's covered bedesten
new.desc: Keskin's old covered bazaar sits in the town centre.
new.tip: Go on market day.
